The Hazel Trophy Competition did not start until 5pm. so that the seniors were able to sit back and watch the Junior competition. In the Junior 100 Clive Ryan and Ken Walker both qualified for the final in which Clive gained 3rd position.
In a Junior match of six events we again won with 23 points to Poly's 22 and Oxford's 18. C. Ryan was first in the 100 yards and 2nd in the 220.

Clive Ryan again brought off the double in the Junior sprints winning the 100 yards in 11.4s. and the 220 yds in 23.3s. Entries were very poor in both these events, only 4 starting in the 100 and 2 in the 220.

Ryan, the father of Clive Ryan, was also present and his help and encouragement to all our lads was much appreciated. He acted as unofficial timekeeper to keep the lads happy about their individual times.
Terry Tupper and Clive Ryan took part in four events achieving a first, two seconds and two third places between them and enabling us to finish third in the 4 x 110yds. relay.
In the absence of Holtum I decided on a gamble and ran Clive Ryan in our senior 4 x 110yds. team.
Most notable were the brilliant doubles of Brian Morris (Sussex 220 & 440 yds.), Ivan Mayers (Middlesex 100 & 220 yds.) and Clive Ryan (Surrey Junior 100 & 220 yds.).

Carter, who was runner up in both sprints, and Clive Ryan, who won both the Junior 100 and 440 yds. Whilst there was no actual scoring, it would seem that the honours were fairly evenly shared by the two teams.
Clive Ryan's time, recorded twice this year, equals Frank Kemp's record set up in July, 1950.

Although entries were only average in number a very fine Championship meeting was held and some really excellent performances were witnessed. Outstanding amongst these were the doubles of Clive Ryan in the 100 and 220 yds. and John Davies in the 880yds and 1 mile.

Our own John Davies, Brian Morris, Clive Ryan, Frank Wright and D. McCorquindale were competing elsewhere, and with Stan Vickers Eric Hall, Norman Caves, Mal Ash and Andorka also unavailable our team could not be said to be truly representative of the name of Belgrave.
On Saturday Clive Ryan and Charlie Jones comfortably qualified for the 440 final despite being drawn against each other in their heat and having to fill first two places.
Most notable of these were the 440 yds. win in 48·7s. by Clive Ryan - a new Championship record, and the mile win of Malcolm Robinson in which Jack Brown's long standing record only just survived.

With 50.2 Clive Ryan qualified for the final, but was unable to reproduce a similar time. With three to qualify in the 880 yards heats both John Thresher and Bob Taylor (Capt) finished fourth in their respective heats.
